thread.title: Apple (AAPL) Reaches Mystical $1 Trillion Market Cap: What Does It Mean?

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Apple (AAPL) Reaches Mystical $1 Trillion Market Cap: What Does It Mean?
text:
Shutterstock photo
It was only a matter of “when” not “if” Apple ( AAPL ) would reach a market cap of $1 trillion. In fact, the conversation soon became which tech company would be the first to achieve the feat? Contenders included FAANG mates Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
In the end, it was Apple, which today by virtue of reaching a stock price of $207.05, garnered a $1 trillion valuation, thanks record-breaking fiscal third quarter results. Apple on Wednesday announced that it had adjusted its number of outstanding shares. This made it easier for the market to know the per-share level needed hit the market cap milestone, which CNBC on Wednesday explained was the $207.05 level.
Apple’s market cap, like those of its aforementioned FAANG peers, has been closely watched since Apple first reached $700 billion a few years ago. For those who are unfamiliar, a company’s market cap essentially is the number of shares the company has when multiplied by the current stock price. But that exact number can fluctuate (sometimes irrationally) when accounting for stock buybacks. It’s for this reason several news outlets aren’t ready to “call” the $1 trillion achievement.
But Apple, which on Tuesday cruised by its Q3 earnings results, can seemingly do no wrong. And the momentum continued through Thursday.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based iPhone maker marveled with $53.3 billion in revenue in its latest quarter, easily topping the $52.3 billion analysts had been looking for. Driven by higher sales of its most-expensive iPhone, Apple also reported earnings per share of $2.34, beating analyst expectations of $2.18.
Notably, Apple blew away revenue and earnings estimates even though it moved “only” 41.3 million iPhones during the quarter, which was less than the 41.79 million Wall Street was expecting. But the company now sells an average iPhone for $724, blowing past the predicted $693.59 average selling price.
Meanwhile, Apple’s services revenue, which includes the App Store and Apple Music as well as iCloud and Apple Pay, raked in a hefty $9.55 billion, beating analyst estimates of $9.2 billion. In terms of forecast, Apple sees Q4 revenue coming the range of $60 billion to $62 billion, beating the $59.6 billion analysts were looking for.
Put all of this together and it Apple, which also announced a cash balance of $243 billion as of the end of the quarter, seemingly has no weaknesses. And this doesn't even mention that the company is in the midst of a $100 billion stock buyback program.
The bottom line is this: The world’s most valuable company just became the first company to hit a trillion dollars. While it’s a tremendous milestone to reach, no one should be surprised. It’s business as usual for Apple, which has done two things better than anyone else: Making great products and making investors wealthy.
